deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page is a longitude determination by the method of lunar distances. The observer's latitude is 51°32' (colatitude 38°28' appears in every triangle), i.e. Göttingen. Paris tables are used ("Pariser Zeit"). The clock is sidereal. The sun's declination is about +15°26' to +15°47', which points to early May. The moon is about 77° east of the sun, i.e. waxing. The final result is a longitude difference of 30m31s in time east of Paris; the modern Göttingen–Paris difference is about 30m26s.

(A) TIME CONVERSION (upper left and middle left).
- The clock reads 6h12'0" at the distance observation. The clock reading at true noon (mural transit, cf. 'Mural 2h48'33"' on the previous page) is 2h48'27.62".
- Elapsed sidereal interval: 6h12'0" − 2h48'27.62" = 3h23'32.38" = 12212.38 s.
- The sun's daily increase in RA is 3m49.6s = 229.6 s ('3.49.6'). The true solar day therefore lasts 24h3m49.6s = 86629.6 sidereal seconds ('24 3 49 6', '86629.6').
- Logarithms: log 229.6 = 2.36097 and log 86629.6 = 4.93767, so log(229.6/86629.6) = 7.42330 − 10.
- Correction: log 12212.38 = 4.08680; 4.08680 + 7.42330 = 1.51010, giving 32.37 s.
- True (apparent solar) time: 3h23'32.38" − 32.37" = 3h23'0.01" ('W.Z.').
- The same procedure is applied at the top to the reading 5h12'0". The interval is 2h23'32.38" = 8612.38 s; log = 3.93512; 3.93512 + 7.42330 → 22.825 s ('22825'). Result: Wahre Zeit 2h23'32.38" − 22.82" = 2h23'9.56".
- Approximate Paris time for the tables. With an assumed longitude of 30m21s: 3h23.0m − 30.35m = 2h52.65m = 2.8775h ('2h8775'). Likewise 2h23'9.6" − 30'21" ≈ 1h52'49" ('Pariser Zeit 1h52'49"').
- The table quantities (moon's RA, declination, parallax; '6.34 = 394"', '3h 197 ... 189') are interpolated to these times. These details are only partly legible.

(B) COMPUTED ALTITUDES. The spherical triangle pole–zenith–body is solved with Napier's analogies. Half-sums and half-differences of the sides are formed and log sin/cos columns follow. Throughout, the colatitude is 90°−φ = 38°28'.
- First epoch (moon): RA 119°13' minus 75°17' gives hour angle t = 43°56'. Declination 15°47', so polar distance 74°13'. Half-sum (74°13'+38°28')/2 = 56°20½'; half-difference 17°52½'. Result: zenith distance 49°54'. My check: cos z = cos38°28'·cos74°13' + sin38°28'·sin74°13'·cos43°56' → z = 49°54.6'.
- Second epoch (moon): RA 121°20' minus 90°17' gives t = 31°3'. Polar distance 74°18'; half-sum 56°23', half-difference 17°55', half-angle 15°31½'. Result: z = 43°32', so altitude b = 46°28' ('21 46 / 43 32'). My check: z = 43°31.8'.
- Sun: t = 90°17' − 39°32' = 50°45' (3h23m of true time). Polar distance 74°34' (decl. ≈ 15°26'); half-sum 56°31', half-difference 18°3'. Result: z ≈ 54°0', so altitude a = 36°0'0". My check: z = 54.0°.

(C) PREPARATION OF THE DISTANCE AND ALTITUDES.
- Observed limb distance: 76°39'36.5".
- Index correction: −3'16", giving 76°36'20.5".
- Added semidiameters and small corrections: +15'53.1" (sun's semidiameter, correct for early May), +15'31.5" (moon, augmented), +20.6".
- This yields the centre distance D. My arithmetic gives 77°8'5.7". The page reads 77°8'47" with heavy overwriting; see errors.
- Moon: horizontal parallax 56'40" (also 56'49"). True altitude B = 46°28'0" + 38'48" = 47°6'48". An earlier attempt subtracting the correction, 45°49'18", is struck out.
- Sun: true altitude A = 36°0'0" − 1'11" (refraction minus parallax) = 35°58'49".

(D) CLEARING THE DISTANCE BY BORDA'S METHOD with an auxiliary angle.
- Inputs: apparent a = 36°0'0", apparent b = 46°28'0", apparent D, true A = 35°58'49", true B = 47°6'48".
- S = (D+a+b)/2: 159°36'47" → 79°48'23½" as written.
- W = (A+B)/2 = 41°32'48½".
- Numerator, log cos S + log cos(S−D) + log cos A + log cos B:
  9.248140 + 9.999530 + 9.908066 + 9.832860 = 8.988596.
- Denominator, log cos a + log cos b + 2 log cos W:
  9.907958 + 9.838078 + 9.748284 = 9.494320 (with log cos W = 9.874142).
- log sin²M = 8.988596 − 9.494320 = 9.494276.
- log sin M = 9.747138 (the transcription has 9.747196), so log cos M = 9.918767.
- log sin(d/2) = log cos W + log cos M = 9.874142 + 9.918767 = 9.792909.
- d/2 = 38°22'13", so the true distance d = 76°44'26".
- This is Borda's formula sin²(d/2) = cos²W − cos S·cos(S−D)·cos A·cos B/(cos a·cos b). It is evaluated as sin(d/2) = cos W·cos M with sin²M = cos S·cos(S−D)·cos A·cos B/(cos a·cos b·cos²W).

(E) PARIS TIME AND LONGITUDE (bottom right).
- The almanac lunar distance changes by 1°30'17" = 5417" per 3h = 10800 s; '1.30.7' suggests a second difference of about 10".
- Interpolation ('4'20"5', '3'59"', '521', '478') gives the Paris time of d = 76°44'26" as 2h52'31". I cannot fully reconstruct this interpolation from the legible figures.
- Longitude: local true time 3h23'0" − Paris time 2h52'3x" = 30'31" east of Paris.
errors: Distance sum: 76°36'20.5" + 15'53.1" + 15'31.5" + 20.6" = 77°8'5.7", not 77°8'47" as transcribed. However, log cos S = 9.248140 corresponds to S ≈ 79°48'2–3", i.e. D ≈ 77°8'6". So Gauss evidently used D ≈ 77°8'6" in the logarithms. The heavily overwritten '47'/'23½' in D, S and the sum 159°36'47" are either misreadings or a correction (47 → 5,7). With 77°8'47" the cleared distance would come out about 40" larger (≈76°45'6").

First block: 5h12'0" − 2h48'37.62" (as transcribed) = 2h23'22.38", whereas the page uses 2h23'32.38". The subtrahend must be 2h48'27.62", as in the second block; this is either a transcription error or a slip of the pen.
Bottom: 3h23'0" − 2h52'31" = 30'29", not 30'31". One of the overwritten seconds figures (Paris time or result) has probably been altered. Paris time 2h52'29" would give 30'31".
Half of 9.494276 is 9.747138, not 9.747196 as transcribed. The subsequent log cos M = 9.918767 corresponds to 9.747138, so this is likely a misreading.

Moon's altitude correction: parallax in altitude 56'40"·cos 46°28' ≈ 39'3" minus refraction ≈ 55" gives ≈ 38'8". The page uses 38'42" (struck) and then 38'48". This differs by about 35–40" from my estimate; the source of the extra amount is unclear, perhaps different parallax or refraction tables.

Conceptual point: the altitudes 46°28' and 36°0' are computed from hour angle and declination, hence geometric/true. Yet in the clearing they are treated as apparent (a, b), with true values A, B derived from them. The struck '45 49 18' (true → apparent) shows Gauss first went the other way. Over-interpretation should be avoided because the page is a working sheet.

The moon's RA moves from 119°13' to 121°20' between the two epochs one hour apart. That is more than the moon's motion of about 33'/h, so the first value was probably rough or refers to something else. Unresolved.

results.what: Conversion of a sidereal clock interval since true noon into apparent solar time, using the sun's daily RA increment (factor 229.6/86629.6)
Altitude of sun and moon from hour angle, declination and latitude, solving the polar triangle with Napier's analogies in logarithms
Clearing a lunar distance: sin²(d/2) = cos²((A+B)/2) − cos S cos(S−D) cos A cos B/(cos a cos b), evaluated with an auxiliary angle M
results.modern_name: Borda's method of clearing the lunar distance

results.what: Longitude from comparing the cleared distance with 3-hourly ephemeris distances (Paris tables); result 30m31s E of Paris, i.e. Göttingen

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine practical-astronomy worksheet: time reduction, computed altitudes, Borda clearing and lunar-distance longitude. Gauss's activity in geographical position determination is well known. The only interest is archival: a Göttingen lunar longitude good to about 5 s of time, and some arithmetic inconsistencies.
transcription_corrections: '2 48 37.62' in the first line is probably 2 48 27.62, which is needed to obtain 2h23'32.38".
'77° 8' 47"', '159 36 47' and '79.48.23½' are heavily overwritten. The logarithms imply D ≈ 77°8'6" and S ≈ 79°48'3".
'36.0.0 / 36.58.49' next to the vertical line should read 36.0.0 / 35.58.49, the true solar altitude A.
'9.494320' under 8.988596 is the sum of the denominator logarithms (log cos a + log cos b + 2 log cos W), not a separate result.
